questions.q: What do you need to do before AutoTune?
options: Nothing: it does everything by itself
Filters and a basic roll/pitch tune
Remove the props and run it on the bench
questions.explain: Filters and the notch, then a manual or QuikTune roll/pitch tune: AutoTune starts from the current gains and aborts when the signal is noisy.

questions.q: INS_HNTCH_MODE = 3 means the notch frequency tracks:
questions.explain: The best mode: it tracks every motor.

questions.q: How do you find the noise frequency for a throttle-based notch?
options: Calculate it from the motor KV and the battery voltage
A raw IMU spectrum in hover
Take it from the prop size
questions.explain: Pre-filter batch sampling or raw IMU logging: INS_LOG_BAT_MASK = 1, OPT = 0, then the spectrum in hover.

questions.q: When are the AutoTune results saved?
options: As soon as each axis finishes in flight

questions.q: What do you do if the motors run hot after AutoTune?
options: Lower I and raise P on all axes
questions.explain: High D on a noisy gyro: filters and the notch, AUTOTUNE_MIN_D, then repeat.
Step 7 is about feel, not stability.

questions.q: Why do you enable the batch sampler before setting up the notch?
options: To see the gyro spectrum before and after the filters
To write the parameters to a file
questions.explain: Batch sampling gives the raw spectrum: you pick the notch frequency from it and verify the result.
